missing_methods.intent: Assert tell your experience text is truncated to characters
missing_methods.query: Assert tell your experience text is truncated to characters
missing_methods.detailed_requirements: This method should verify that the text entered in the 'tell your experience' field is truncated to a maximum number of characters. Steps: 1) Retrieve the current text from the feedback text field using get_entered_text() or similar method. 2) Get the character count display using get_feedback_text_char_count() if available. 3) Assert that the length of the entered text does not exceed the expected_max_length parameter. 4) Return True if the assertion passes, False otherwise. 5) Should handle edge cases where text might be empty or exactly at the limit. 6) May need to parse the character count display text to extract numeric values for validation.
missing_methods.rationale: While feedback.py has methods to input text (input_tell_your_experience) and get character count (get_feedback_text_char_count), there is no explicit method to assert that the text is truncated to a specific character limit. This validation logic belongs in feedback.py as it directly relates to the feedback form's text input constraints.

Calculate the actual character length using len(entered_text)

Call existing get_feedback_text_char_count(timeout=10) method to retrieve the character count display text
Parse the character count display text to extract the current count and max count (e.g., '1500/2000' format)
Assert that len(entered_text) equals the parsed current count from the character count display
Assert that the parsed max count from the character count display equals expected_max_length
Handle edge case: if entered_text is empty (length 0), verify character count display shows '0/{expected_max_length}'
Handle edge case: if entered_text length equals expected_max_length, verify no additional characters can be entered
